title: Tom Anderson's place, its management and bootleg liquor
summary: Tom Anderson was boss of the district; the band was paid with no instruction; liquor was served in milk bottles; singer Willie Jackson.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I was reading the show in New Orleans. The French Quarter. Yeah, everything. What kind of a place was Tom Anderson's? Was it a pretty big place at Cabaret? He was there, he had a swell place.

He had lead of the town. Anything he wanted he did there. I heard he was the boss of the district. He was great, yeah. And the way he sees place, all of all were looking glass. Anywhere you go they could see it. Oh really?
Yeah, he had a swell place, yeah.

Well years I have to give up, he had his son lost to run a father named George Delsick. Oh yeah, I heard it. Used to run it, yeah. Used to run it. I worked there a long time for him. He was a nice friend. You never know, he'd never tell the band nothing. Never tell the band nothing. They'd give you a $5 bill, but don't take a dollar for him. You had to share the straight place. He'd never say nothing.
That was Tom bootlegging time too.
Yeah. Yeah. They served liquor there. Oh yeah. They'd get it for you.
Yeah. See them fellas take a milk bottle, you know, painted white, you know. Yeah. Put whiskey in there, they couldn't see if they'd take it for milk.
They did that. I never heard of that. Pretty good idea. They did that at Tom Anderson's. Right. They had some fun around there.
And they had entertainers like singers, you say.
Yeah, they had a singer, that's an entertainer, yeah. Yeah. Had a fella by, you know what I'd talk to him, Willie Jackson. Oh yeah.
He made some records once with the- Yeah.
I never met him, but I have some of his records.
